questions.question: Which presentation requires urgent evaluation for possible septic arthritis?
choices: Acute hot swollen knee with fever and severe pain on motion
Stable chronic hand stiffness
A routine DMARD refill request
Mild activity-related knee crepitus
questions.explanation: An acutely hot swollen joint with systemic symptoms and severe pain can represent septic arthritis and needs urgent in-person assessment.

questions.question: Why does absence of fever not safely rule out septic arthritis?
choices: Older or immunosuppressed patients may not have fever despite infection
Septic arthritis never causes fever
Only RA causes joint warmth
Laboratory tests replace assessment
questions.explanation: Fever may be absent in septic arthritis, particularly in older or immunosuppressed patients; the total presentation determines urgency.

questions.question: Which pattern supports possible inflammatory arthritis?
choices: Warm swollen joints with prolonged morning stiffness and symmetric small-joint symptoms
Pain only after a single injury
Brief stiffness after sitting with no swelling
Stable painless bony enlargement only
questions.explanation: Inflammatory arthritis often has synovitis, prolonged stiffness, rest symptoms, fatigue, and multi-joint/symmetric involvement.

questions.question: Why is early rheumatology referral important in suspected persistent inflammatory polyarthritis?
choices: Early disease-modifying treatment can reduce inflammation and help prevent joint damage
Referral removes the need for examination
Only severe deformity warrants referral
Symptomatic analgesics prevent erosions
questions.explanation: Prompt rheumatology assessment and DMARD-directed care can limit progressive joint damage and disability.

questions.question: How should rheumatoid factor or anti-CCP testing be interpreted?
choices: With clinical pattern, examination, timeline, and other evaluation—not as a stand-alone diagnosis
A positive test always proves RA
A negative test excludes all inflammatory arthritis
Testing replaces referral
questions.explanation: Serologies support but do not independently establish or exclude inflammatory arthritis; clinical context is essential.

questions.question: What is an FNP safety responsibility for a patient on a DMARD or biologic?
choices: Confirm the medication plan, monitoring, infection precautions, adherence, access, and laboratory/referral follow-up
Continue therapy without reviewing symptoms
Ignore vaccination planning
Treat every fever as an ordinary flare
questions.explanation: Immunomodulating treatment needs coordinated monitoring, infection awareness, medication reconciliation, and follow-up ownership.

questions.question: Why should suspected significant infection be communicated to the prescribing rheumatology team?
choices: Immunomodulating therapy may require individualized interruption or adjustment and the patient needs coordinated acute care
Every infection proves the medication is ineffective
The patient should self-adjust all medications
Infection is unrelated to RA therapy
questions.explanation: Possible infection requires prompt clinical assessment and coordination with the prescribing team; patients should not self-manage complex immunosuppression.

questions.question: What is a risk of repeated long-term glucocorticoid exposure?
choices: Infection, hyperglycemia, hypertension, osteoporosis, mood effects, and adrenal suppression
Permanent prevention of all joint damage
No systemic effects
Elimination of monitoring needs
questions.explanation: Glucocorticoids can be useful in limited settings but have substantial long-term adverse effects and do not replace disease-modifying care.

questions.question: Which domain belongs in longitudinal RA follow-up?
choices: Function, fatigue, cardiovascular risk, vaccines, mood, work impact, falls, and medication access
Only joint x-rays
Only a pain score
Only the next prescription date
questions.explanation: RA is systemic and functionally disruptive; follow-up should include comorbidity, prevention, psychosocial, and access assessment.

questions.question: What is the FNP-level inflammatory arthritis principle?
choices: Assume every new painful joint is an RA flare
Exclude urgent infection, refer persistent inflammatory disease early, and support safe function-focused treatment
Use steroids as the entire long-term plan
Ignore extra-articular disease
questions.explanation: High-quality care balances emergency recognition, prompt rheumatology collaboration, medication safety, and whole-person function.
